title: Bowel obstruction and ileus in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the bowel obstruction or ileus (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Acute abdominal pain, suspected bowel obstruction.

Vitals:
T: 98.6 F, HR: 88, BP: 130/82, RR: 18, SpO2: 96% on RA.

Recent Labs:
WBC: 12.4 (elevated)
Hgb: 11.8
Hct: 35.2%
Na: 138
K: 4.1
Cr: 1.1
eGFR: 65
Lactic Acid: 1.8

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Fatigue, mild nausea.
GI: Severe abdominal pain, distension, no emesis.
MSK: No joint pain.
Neuro: Alert and oriented x3.
Skin: NAD.

Social History: Retired, lives with daughter. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol.
Family History: Mother had hypertension. Father had stroke.
Hospital Course:
Pt is an 80-year-old female admitted with acute onset severe abdominal pain and distension. Imaging confirmed a complete small bowel obstruction. Clinical evaluation and history revealed the etiology was due to adhesions from a prior abdominal surgery. Pt was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and NG tube decompression initially. Due to lack of improvement, pt underwent emergency surgical release of adhesions. Procedure was successful with resolution of the obstruction. Postop course was uncomplicated; pt tolerated diet progression well. Pain managed with scheduled and PRN medications. Pt stable for discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Complete small bowel obstruction
Adhesions

Discharge Medications:
1. Acetaminophen 650mg BID PRN for pain.
2. Multivitamin daily.
3. Stool softener daily.

Follow-up:
F/u with General Surgery in 2 weeks for wound check and progress.

Electronically signed,
T. Haddad, MD
05/18/2026
explanations: Intestinal adhesions with complete obstruction: K56.52 (HCC 78).
